title: The same with numeric positions
summary: Command a two-axis assembler with numeric setpoints in centimetres and a position tolerance instead of limit switches.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Send an axis to a named position with a setpoint and read its position back.
Decide that a move is done when the position is within a tolerance of the setpoint, not when it is equal to it.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/Assembler.st, the pad works at four positions (lid belt x 0, base belt x 100, down y 0, safe height y 30), and a move is done when the pad is within 0.2 cm of its target.
stages.checkpoint: Each move ends only when the pad is close enough to its target; the pad never crosses the belts below the safe height.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the numbers for one lid: y goes to 30, x to 0, y to 0, the vacuum grips, y to 30, x to 100, y to 0, the vacuum lets go, y to 30 and x back to 0.
stages.checkpoint: XPos and YPos reach each setpoint within 0.2 cm before the next state starts; the vacuum is on only between the grip and the release.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}: The starter commands no position, so the pad stays where it is; send it to the lid, grip, carry the lid to the base and release it, three times, and light Green after the third.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press {{ui:toolbar.run.label}} (F5) and open the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named two-axis-assembly-numeric and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch XPos and YPos in the trace come to each setpoint, and the pad in the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}} cross the belts only at the safe height.
stages.checkpoint: A lid is set on each base, nothing is dropped, and Green is on at the end.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: A position is a measurement, so a comparison with a tolerance is the correct test; an exact equality of two REAL values can fail forever. The scenario proves that an assembly was made and delivered, that nothing was dropped and that Green is on at the end. It cannot read a position value, so it does not check your tolerance or your setpoints.
stages.checkpoint: What the assertions check is tested; nothing else is.

hints.text: Look at how the pad reaches a setpoint: its position is a REAL that comes close to the setpoint but may never equal it. Each state must wait for a flag that says the pad is near enough.

Write XAt := ABS(XPos - XSet) < Tol; and the same for Y, and let each state change only when its At flag is TRUE. Raise to the safe height first, then move in X, then lower; set the setpoint when you enter the state, not on every scan of a state that waits. Constants: LidX 0.0, BaseX 100.0, Down 0.0, Safe 30.0, Tol 0.2. The steps, each with its exit condition and what it sets: 0 idle, on Start YSet := Safe, to 1; 1 when YAt, XSet := LidX, to 2; 2 when XAt, to 3; 3 when LidReady and BaseReady and the last base has left, to 4; 4 after a TON SettleT of T#800ms, YSet := Down, to 5; 5 when YAt, to 6; 6 after a TON GripT of T#400ms and Gripped, YSet := Safe, to 7; 7 when YAt, XSet := BaseX, to 8; 8 when XAt, YSet := Down, to 9; 9 when YAt, to 10; 10 after a TON LetGoT of T#400ms, YSet := Safe, Cycles := Cycles + 1 and FreeBase := TRUE, to 11; 11 when YAt, XSet := LidX, to 12; 12 when XAt, to 13 once Cycles >= 3, otherwise back to 3. Outputs: Grip while the step is 6 to 9; Start latches Active, and RunLid, RunBase, RunExit and HoldLid follow Active; HoldBase is Active AND NOT FreeBase; Green is step 13; Amber is Active and not step 13. Feeding: a R_TRIG Go on Start, an F_TRIG LidGone on LidReady and a TON BaseLeft of T#600ms on FreeBase AND NOT BaseReady; EmitLid := (Go.Q OR LidGone.Q) AND Active AND LidsFed < 3; EmitBase := (Go.Q OR BaseLeft.Q) AND Active AND BasesFed < 3; count each emit, and clear FreeBase when BaseLeft.Q is TRUE. The code of one step: ELSIF Step = 1 AND YAt THEN XSet := LidX; Step := 2;

faultCases: The starter commands no position, so the pad stays where it is; send it to the lid, grip, carry the lid to the base and release it, three times, and light Green after the third.
